issues.legal_issue: A later notice issued after termination of a lease does not waive the earlier termination unless the authority intentionally relinquished a known right.
material_facts: The lease was cancelled by the State Government before the Collector issued the later notice.
The later notice concerned subsequent breaches and was issued without the Collector knowing that the lease had already been cancelled.
The Collector had no power to revive the terminated lease.
There was no intentional abandonment by the State Government of its decision to terminate the lease.
issues.conclusion: The later notice did not waive the earlier cancellation.
issues.legal_principle: Waiver requires the voluntary and intentional relinquishment of a known right or advantage. The Court observed that estoppel generally does not operate against the State in the exercise of governmental, public, sovereign, legislative, or executive powers, relying on Excise Commissioner v. Ramkumar, 1976 Supp. SCR 532, and American Jurisprudence, 2nd ed., paragraph 123, page 783. The dispute arose under Rule 27(5) of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, governing notice and termination for a lessee's breach.

rule.if: lease_cancellation_appeal and lease_terminated_before_later_notice and later_notice_issued_without_knowledge_of_termination and no_intentional_relinquishment

predicates.lease_cancellation_appeal: The proceeding challenges the termination of a lease following alleged breaches of its conditions.
predicates.lease_terminated_before_later_notice: The responsible authority terminated the lease before a later notice concerning breaches was issued.
predicates.later_notice_issued_without_knowledge_of: The official who issued the later notice did so without knowing that the lease had already been terminated.
predicates.no_intentional_relinquishment: The responsible authority did not voluntarily and intentionally give up a known right or advantage.

issues.definition: When a lease-termination appeal involves a later notice issued without knowledge of an already effective termination and no intentional relinquishment, the earlier termination is not treated as waived.

issues.legal_issue: Natural justice does not require a personal hearing where the affected party has had a fair opportunity to respond in writing and the response does not dispute the breach but seeks only condonation.
material_facts: The leaseholder received notice specifying breaches, including unpaid amounts and failure to install a weighing machine.
The leaseholder responded by acknowledging the breach and seeking condonation, rather than disputing the material facts.
The facts were simple, and the leaseholder had an opportunity to present the explanation relied upon.
A later notice offered a personal hearing, but that offer related to the later notice, not the earlier cancellation.
issues.conclusion: Natural justice was complied with; the absence of a personal hearing before the earlier cancellation did not invalidate the decision.
issues.legal_principle: The requirements of natural justice are flexible and cannot be fitted into rigid forms; their application depends on the circumstances, including whether the affected party had a just opportunity to state its case. In the context of Rule 27(5) of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, the Court held that the lessee's response to the notice provided an adequate opportunity in the circumstances.

rule.if: lease_cancellation_appeal and notice_specified_breaches and written_response_opportunity and response_only_sought_condonation and no_material_dispute_about_breach

predicates.lease_cancellation_appeal: The proceeding challenges termination of a lease following alleged breaches of its conditions.
predicates.notice_specified_breaches: The affected leaseholder received notice identifying the alleged breaches.
predicates.written_response_opportunity: The leaseholder had an opportunity to respond to the notice in writing.
predicates.response_only_sought_condonation: The response acknowledged the breach and sought that it be excused rather than contesting it.
predicates.no_material_dispute_about_breach: The material facts establishing the breach were not disputed.

issues.definition: Where a leaseholder facing termination received notice, could respond in writing, and only sought condonation of an undisputed breach, natural justice is satisfied without a separate personal hearing.

issues.legal_issue: A revisional decision is not invalid merely because it refers to matters in a later notice when the affected party itself raised those matters and their consideration caused no prejudice.
material_facts: The leaseholder's revision challenged the cancellation made following the first notice.
In additional submissions, the leaseholder referred to the later notice.
The revisional authority's order referred to matters in that later notice.
The Court found that the leaseholder had suffered no prejudice from the reference.
issues.conclusion: The revisional decision was not invalidated by its reference to matters in the later notice.
issues.legal_principle: A decision is not vitiated by consideration of material introduced by the affected party where the decision causes no prejudice. The Court considered the revisional authority's exercise of power under Rule 55 of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, and found no merit in the allegation that the later-notice matters were extraneous.

predicates.lease_cancellation_revision: The proceeding is a revision challenging a lease cancellation decision.
predicates.affected_party_raised_later_notice_matte: The affected party itself brought matters from a later notice to the revisional authority's attention.
predicates.revisional_authority_referred_to_those_m: The authority reviewing the cancellation referred to those later-notice matters in its decision.
predicates.no_prejudice_from_reference: The reference to the later-notice matters caused no prejudice to the affected party.

issues.definition: In a lease-cancellation revision, the authority's reference to later-notice matters does not invalidate its decision when the affected party raised those matters and suffered no prejudice.

issues.legal_issue: A court should not interfere with a discretionary lease-cancellation decision in the absence of a special feature that vitiates the exercise of discretion.
material_facts: The leaseholder admitted breaches of lease conditions and obligations under the applicable rules.
The leaseholder sought excuse or condonation of those breaches.
The competent authority exercised its discretion to cancel the lease and forfeit the security deposit.
The Court found no special feature vitiating the exercise of discretion.
issues.conclusion: The discretionary decision was not set aside, although the leaseholder remained free to seek reconsideration from the State Government.
issues.legal_principle: The Court will not ordinarily interfere with a discretionary exercise of power in the absence of special vitiating features. The discretion to terminate and forfeit arose under Rule 27(5) of the Mineral Concession Rules, 1960, which permits termination and forfeiture when a breach is not remedied after notice.

rule.if: lease_cancellation_appeal and breach_admitted and decision_made_in_exercise_of_discretion and no_special_vitiating_feature

predicates.lease_cancellation_appeal: The proceeding challenges a decision terminating a lease following breaches of its conditions.
predicates.breach_admitted: The leaseholder acknowledged the material breach rather than disputing it.
predicates.decision_made_in_exercise_of_discretion: The competent authority chose to terminate the lease and impose the associated consequence using its discretionary power.
predicates.no_special_vitiating_feature: No special circumstance was established that would vitiate the authority's exercise of discretion.

issues.definition: When a lease-cancellation appeal concerns an admitted breach and a discretionary decision with no special vitiating feature, the decision is not set aside.
